names.official: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe

summary: São Tomé and Príncipe waives visas for short visits — citizens of the EU, US, UK, Canada and the Portuguese-speaking CPLP countries can stay visa-free for up to 15 days — while other nationalities apply online for an eVisa before arrival.

payments.text: Cards are accepted at only a few hotels in the capital. Bring cash. The dobra is pegged to the euro, and euros are widely accepted or easily exchanged; ATMs are few and often empty.

safety.text: São Tomé and Príncipe is one of Africa’s safest destinations, with little violent crime. Take normal care with valuables on beaches and at night in the capital.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The gravana dry season from June to September is the classic window, with a shorter dry spell in January and February — both suit beaches, hiking and whale- or turtle-watching seasons.

tips.text: The visa waiver covers only 15 days — if you plan a longer stay, apply for the eVisa before traveling or arrange an extension with the Migration and Border Service soon after arrival.
Bring enough cash in euros for your whole stay — ATMs are scarce and unreliable, cards are rarely accepted, and euros are exchanged everywhere at the fixed peg.
International flights are few (mainly via Lisbon, Accra, Libreville and Luanda) and inter-island flights to Príncipe sell out. Book early and reconfirm, as schedules change at short notice.
Malaria has been greatly reduced but still occurs. Use repellent and nets, and consider prophylaxis for longer or rural stays.
Services run on “léve-léve” (easy-easy) island time. Allow slack in your plans, carry some patience, and settle prices for taxis and guides before setting off.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: Citizens of the EU and Schengen area, the US, UK, Canada and the Portuguese-speaking CPLP countries do not need a visa for stays of up to 15 days. Everyone else — and anyone staying longer — applies online for an eVisa on the official Smart Visa portal (smart.st) before arrival.

faq.question: How can I stay longer than 15 days?
faq.answer: Apply for the eVisa before traveling (typically allowing stays of up to 30 days) or request an extension from the Migration and Border Service in São Tomé before your permitted stay expires.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — which covers most nearby mainland departure points such as Gabon, Angola or Ghana. Arriving directly from Europe, no certificate is needed, but carry the yellow card if your routing touches the mainland.

faq.question: What money should I bring to São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: Cash, ideally euros. The dobra is pegged to the euro and euros are accepted or exchanged everywhere, while ATMs are few and cards work only at a handful of hotels.

faq.question: How do I get to São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: By air only for practical purposes. The main links are Lisbon (TAP), plus regional connections such as Accra, Libreville and Luanda. Book early: frequencies are low and the onward hop to Príncipe island is a small plane that fills quickly.
